title: Beta-blockers for heart failure with reduced, mid-range, and preserved ejection fraction: an individual patient-level analysis of double-blind randomized trials
authors: Cleland JGF, Bunting KV, Flather MD, Altman DG, Holmes J, Coats AJS, et al.; Beta-blockers in Heart Failure Collaborative Group
population: Individual patient data on 18,637 patients from 11 double-blind placebo-controlled trials of beta-blockers in heart failure, stratified by baseline ejection fraction and rhythm after exclusion of missing electrocardiogram or ejection fraction, heart block and paced rhythm: 14,262 patients in sinus rhythm (median ejection fraction 27%, 575 with 40% to 49% and 244 with 50% or more) and 3050 in atrial fibrillation
funder: Menarini Farmaceutica Internazionale provided an unrestricted research grant for administrative costs; GlaxoSmithKline provided data extraction support; IRCCS San Raffaele provided a collaborative research grant. One author is funded through a National Institute for Health Research Career Development Fellowship (CDF-2015-08-074) that also supports a second author. The acknowledgements thank AstraZeneca, GlaxoSmithKline, Menarini Farmaceutica and Merck Serono for full access to trial data, and BEST data came through the NHLBI BioLINCC programme.
authorConflicts: Several authors report fees or grants from Amgen, Novartis, AstraZeneca and other companies; listed in the paper.
result: In sinus rhythm, all-cause mortality hazard ratios with beta-blockers against placebo were 0.70 (95% CI 0.60 to 0.83) at ejection fraction below 20% (623 deaths among 2531), 0.76 (0.65 to 0.89) at 20% to 25%, 0.75 (0.64 to 0.88) at 26% to 34%, 0.67 (0.50 to 0.90) at 35% to 39%, 0.59 (0.34 to 1.03) at 40% to 49% (21 of 292 against 35 of 283 died; cardiovascular death 13 of 292 against 26 of 283, hazard ratio 0.48, 0.24 to 0.97) and 1.79 (0.78 to 4.10) at 50% or more (24 deaths among 241). In atrial fibrillation, beta-blockers raised ejection fraction when below 50% but did not improve prognosis: all-cause mortality hazard ratios 1.23 (0.88 to 1.74) below 20%, 0.74 (0.54 to 1.02) at 20% to 25%, 0.98 (0.74 to 1.29) at 26% to 34%, 0.92 (0.53 to 1.58) at 35% to 39% and 1.30 (0.63 to 2.67) at 40% to 49%.
